title:
Space engineering
Ground systems and operations
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-70C Working Group)
status_notes: Issue of 31 July 2008. It is the evolution of ECSS-E-70 Part 1A (25 April 2000, principles and requirements) and Part 2A (2 April 2001, document requirements definitions), now published together; ECSS-E-70B was never issued (change log, p. 3). The change log does not give an issue name for the C version. The document does not state that it is superseded, and no later issue is in the library.
summary:
The top-level ECSS standard for the **ground segment and mission operations**. It gives the rules, principles and requirements for engineering the ground segment and for preparing and carrying out operations. It also covers the customer relationships with the ground segment supplier (GSS) and with the operations supplier (OS). EGSE for spacecraft verification and the launch segment are excluded.

Clause 4 defines the domain. Operations organizations (teams of operations managers, spacecraft controllers, flight dynamics engineers and others) together with ground systems form *entities*. The ground segment consists of the mission operations system (monitoring and control, flight dynamics, planning, simulation, OBSW maintenance, archiving), the payload operations and data system, the ground station system and the ground communications system.

Clauses 5 and 6 are written as process chains with inputs, requirements and outputs:

* **operations engineering**: requirements analysis and concept (MOCD, SSORD tailored from ECSS-E-ST-70-11, on-board services selected from ECSS-E-ST-70-41), mission operations data production (MOP, procedures, and **monitoring and control databases** populated with TM/TC, display and OBCP definitions), data validation against an operational simulator (System Validation Tests), team training, operational validation, configuration management, execution and disposal;
* **ground segment engineering**: definition, production, AIT and verification, maintenance and disposal.

Clause 7 maps these processes onto phases A to F and their reviews (GSSRR, GSPDR, GSCDR, GSQR, ORR, FRR, IOOR, ELR, MCR). Normative Annexes A to J give the DRDs: CRD, MAR, MOCD, OEP, SSUM, OVP, MOP, OAR, operations procedures and CFISRD. Annex K discusses reuse (common M&C databases between AIT and operations), and Annex L lists the Level-3 standards ECSS-E-ST-70-01, -11, -31, -32 and -41.

key_points.text: Main changes from ECSS-E-70A: a process approach separating operations engineering from ground segment engineering, separate customer-supplier relationships for each, harmonization with ECSS-E-ST-10C, no assumed reference architecture, DRDs as normative annexes, and new DRDs MAR, MOP, CFISRD, OEP and SEP.
Scope excludes ground systems (e.g. EGSE) and operations supporting space segment verification, covered by ECSS-E-ST-10-02, and the launch segment and its operations.

A synthetic parameter is a parameter derived from telemetry and other data via an algorithm; mission operations data are the subset of mission information used to execute in-orbit operations (e.g. procedures, operations rules, monitoring and control databases).
The ground segment typically comprises the mission operations system, the payload operations and data system, the ground station system and the ground communications system.

The mission operations system supports mission analysis, operations preparation, simulation, planning and scheduling, monitoring and control, flight dynamics, on-board software maintenance, data archiving, user services, data product delivery, performance analysis, configuration management and system maintenance.

The ground station system provides TM reception, storage and distribution, TC transmission, tracking/ranging/Doppler/meteo data acquisition, station monitoring and control, time management, network management and data distribution.
Critical areas include reuse of space segment operations knowledge and data (e.g. telemetry and telecommand definitions, procedures) between space segment design, AIT and mission operations.

Space segment operability requirements are compiled in the SSORD, a tailored version of ECSS-E-ST-70-11; the on-board mission operations services, their capability sets and the corresponding telecommands and telemetry are defined with the operations customer, tailoring ECSS-E-ST-70-41.

Inputs to mission operations data production include the SSUM and the space segment monitoring and control database (from the operations customer) and the ground segment monitoring and control database (from the ground segment supplier).

Ground system monitoring and control databases shall be populated with mission-specific data, including mission planning data, OBCPs, telemetry and telecommand definitions, display definitions, on-board software images and patches.
Table 7-8 lists the key ground segment and operations documents and the reviews at which each is deliverable.

Mission operations data are validated with tools representative of the space segment, mainly an operational simulator, and on a flight-representative space segment exercising all procedures, telecommands, modes and redundancies (System Validation Tests).

Table 7-9 defines the ground segment and operations reviews with their purpose, timing and owner, e.g. GSSRR (phase B), GSPDR (end of phase B), GSCDR (end of phase C), GSQR (phase D), ORR (end of phase D, operations customer), ELR (end of phase E2) and MCR (end of phase F).

Annex K recommends reuse of monitoring and control databases and displays between spacecraft manufacturer, check-out and operations, and commonality between EGSE and ground station space link functions (downlink reception, uplink radiation, downlink and uplink data processing).

Annex L lists the level 3 standards: ECSS-E-ST-70-01 (OBCPs), -11 (space segment operability), -31 (monitoring and control data definition, Space System Model), -32 (procedure language, PLUTO) and -41 (PUS).
